objective: Quantify borough-level NYC yellow-taxi travel patterns and demand change from January to February 2024, and identify the borough with the largest absolute increase in average total fare (Feb - Jan).
key_questions: How do average trip distance, average total fare and trip volume differ by pickup borough between Jan-2024 and Feb-2024?
Which borough shows the largest absolute increase in average total fare from January to February 2024?

trip_data.note: ~2.96M rows, 48.8 MB parquet -> must read column subset via pandas.read_parquet(columns=...)

schema.passenger_count: float64 (140,162 nulls in Jan; not used)

zone_lookup.encoding_note: read with encoding='utf-8-sig' and strip BOM/whitespace from column names
zone_lookup.shapefile_note: taxi_zones/taxi_zones.shp has no .dbf attribute table (geometry only, 263 records) -> cannot be used for LocationID->Borough; use the CSV lookup.

issues: Negative fare_amount: 37,448 rows (Jan) / 40,655 rows (Feb); min -899 / -999 -> removed by fare >= 0 bound.
Extreme positive values: trip_distance max 312,722 mi (Jan) / 222,478 mi (Feb); fare_amount/total_amount max 5,000 (Jan) / 9,792 (Feb) -> removed by upper bounds.
No nulls in trip_distance / fare_amount / total_amount / PULocationID; passenger_count has 140,162 / ~nulls (unused).
Out-of-file-month pickup datetimes (~30 rows, e.g. 2002-12, 2009-01, 2023-12, 2024-03): keep (task only specifies distance/fare filters); sensitivity note in robustness.
Zones labelled Unknown / N/A or not present in lookup (~11.8k Jan + ~10.9k Feb trips) -> excluded from borough aggregation.
Total drop rate from filters: 1.27% (Jan) / 1.35% (Feb) -> acceptable.

filters.null_handling: drop rows with null trip_distance, fare_amount, total_amount, PULocationID

transformation_steps.action: Read each parquet with the 5 needed columns only (pandas.read_parquet(columns=...)); never print raw frames.
Apply inclusive filters 0<=trip_distance<=100 and 0<=fare_amount<=1000 plus null drops; record before/after row counts.
Map PULocationID -> Borough via taxi_zone_lookup.csv; restrict to the 6 valid borough labels (drop Unknown/N/A/unmapped).
Tag month from the source file (1 = Jan-2024, 2 = Feb-2024).
Group by (borough, month): mean(trip_distance) as avg_trip_distance, mean(total_amount) as avg_total_fare, size as trip_count.
Pivot to wide per borough: absolute_increase = avg_total_fare(month 2) - avg_total_fare(month 1); broadcast the value to both monthly rows of the borough.
is_max_increase = (borough's absolute_increase == max over boroughs of absolute_increase); True on both rows of the winning borough, False otherwise.
Round floats to 4 decimals, trip_count to int; write output1.json sorted by borough then month.
Build grouped bar chart (Jan vs Feb) with the two required subplots from output1.json; save output2.png at dpi>=150.

metric_definitions.avg_trip_distance: mean of trip_distance (miles) over filtered trips of that borough-month (pickup-borough basis)
metric_definitions.avg_total_fare: mean of total_amount (USD) over filtered trips of that borough-month
metric_definitions.trip_count: number of filtered trips (demand volume proxy) of that borough-month
metric_definitions.absolute_increase: avg_total_fare(Feb 2024) - avg_total_fare(Jan 2024) for the borough, in USD (signed; negative = decrease)
metric_definitions.is_max_increase: boolean flag on the borough with the largest (most positive) absolute_increase; applied to both of its month rows

interpretation_decision.chosen: largest positive absolute change in average total fare (max of Feb - Jan)
interpretation_decision.rationale: task says 'largest absolute increase' -> an increase, measured in absolute USD rather than percent; the magnitude-only alternative is reported as a sensitivity check, because with this filter it selects a decrease (EWR -$10.65).

magnitude_only_max.note: a decrease, not an increase; small sample (284/279 trips)

sensitivity.conclusion: Bronx stays the largest increase under every variant tested.

expected_reference_results.note: reference values already computed in data_profile.json/analysis_summary (used only as a consistency check for the execution node)

output1.json.format: JSON array of objects, one per (borough, month) = 6 boroughs x 2 months = 12 objects

fields.name: borough
fields.note: Manhattan, Queens, Brooklyn, Bronx, Staten Island, EWR

fields.name: absolute_increase
fields.note: Feb - Jan, same value on both rows of a borough

fields.name: is_max_increase
fields.note: True only for the winning borough (Bronx expected), on both of its rows

output2.png.type: matplotlib figure, 2 subplots side by side, Agg backend, dpi>=150

left_subplot.content: grouped bars Jan vs Feb 2024 of avg_trip_distance per borough
left_subplot.graph_title: Average Trip Distance by Borough (Jan vs Feb 2024)
left_subplot.detail: x ticks = borough names (rotated for readability), legend Jan 2024 / Feb 2024, value labels on bars

right_subplot.content: grouped bars Jan vs Feb 2024 of avg_total_fare per borough
right_subplot.graph_title: Average Total Fare by Borough (Jan vs Feb 2024)
right_subplot.detail: same borough order as left subplot for comparability; value labels on bars

validation_checks: sum(trip_count over months) == rows_used_total (5,871,132 by reference profile)
output1.json has exactly 12 records, each borough appears exactly twice (month 1 and 2)
exactly one borough has is_max_increase == true, and it equals argmax(absolute_increase)
absolute_increase identical on both monthly rows of every borough and consistent with rounded fare difference (tolerance 1e-3)
all avg_trip_distance in [0,100], all avg_total_fare in [0,1000]; trip_count > 0
output2.png exists, >50 KB, contains both required titles and axis labels (verify by re-reading strings in the plotting script / image size)
risks_and_caveats: EWR is a lookup 'Borough' value but not one of the 5 NYC boroughs and has a tiny sample (284 / 279 trips): its averages are volatile and drive the magnitude-only alternative.
Staten Island also tiny (68 / 54 trips) -> unstable change (-$4.67).
Borough is assigned by pickup zone only; trips are not split/shared between boroughs.
Trip counts differ between months (Feb has ~1.4% more raw rows), so averages - not counts - are the reliable comparison; counts are reported as demand volume.
Rounding to 4 decimals may make very small differences ambiguous (Bronx +0.8024 vs Manhattan +0.2862 are far apart, so ranking is safe).

Environment note: this planning node's isolated interpreter has pandas but no pyarrow/matplotlib; the execution steps require an interpreter with pyarrow (parquet IO) and matplotlib (PNG), as already assumed by scripts/*.py.
